name: Intermediate Bodybuilding Program (Muscle & Strength Pyramid)
author: Eric Helms, Andy Morgan, Andrea Valdez
summary: A five-day Lower / Upper / Lower / Push / Pull program from the Muscle and Strength Pyramid authors, with compound lifts wave-loaded over 3-week waves and isolation work on double progression. Every fourth week is an optional deload decided by a short fatigue checklist.
evidenceNote: Most muscles get about 10-16 sets per week across two sessions at roughly 2 RIR on the first set, squarely in the evidence-based range for intermediates. Wave loading gives built-in heavy-to-moderate variation and planned fatigue management. Weak points: direct side-delt work is absent (overhead presses and face pulls only), and the 4x3-5 squat and deadlift on the same day is demanding.

sources.title: Intermediate Bodybuilding Program (RippedBody.com, Andy Morgan, updated 28 Dec 2025)
Intermediate Bodybuilding Program by Eric Helms (Boostcamp, official Muscle and Strength Pyramid account)

schedule: Day 1 Lower, Day 2 Upper, Day 3 Lower, Day 4 Push, Day 5 Pull, once each per week; RippedBody advises training no more than three days in a row. Boostcamp stores weekdays as indices 1,2,4,5,6, most likely Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat (index mapping not stated, so unverified). Run the 4-week block (3 loading weeks + optional deload) three times for 12 weeks, then repeat.

progression.description: Exercises, sets and rep ranges match the authors' RippedBody page (updated 28 Dec 2025; sample program from the 2nd edition of The Muscle and Strength Pyramid: Training) and the official Boostcamp version. First-set target is 2 RIR (= RPE 8); use the same weight for the remaining sets (Boostcamp). Compounds and 8-12 accessories wave-load (Boostcamp description): start at a weight where all sets hit the top of the range without failing; each following week add load and drop one rep per set (two reps for 8-12 ranges), e.g. 3-5: 5/4/3, 4-6: 6/5/4, 5-7: 7/6/5, 6-8: 8/7/6, 8-12: 12/10/8. Load step: Boostcamp week notes say +5 kg (10 lb) per week for barbell squat and deadlift and +2.5 kg (5 lb) for every other exercise, including lower-body accessories; the incrementKg.lower value of 5 applies only to squat and deadlift. Deload week uses the lowest weight (week 1) and lowest reps (week 3) of the block with about one third fewer sets. The next block starts at week-1 reps, 2.5 kg (5 kg for squat/deadlift) heavier than the previous block's week 1. 12-15 isolation slots (seated calf raise, flys, face pulls) use double progression: start with a load close to but short of 15 reps on every set, add reps each session until every set reaches 15, then add weight and restart lower. RippedBody itself gives only a simpler rule (add a little weight whenever you can, then switch to autoregulated double progression) and points to the book for the wave details.
progression.deload: Optional deload every 4th week (weeks 4, 8, 12). Checklist: dreading the gym? sleeping worse than normal? loads/reps decreasing? stress worse than normal? aches and pains worse than normal? Yes to 2 or more = deload: cut sets by about one third and use the lowest weight and reps of the previous 3 weeks. Yes to 0-1 = skip it and start the next block.
